Create an corner with two 140x140 plates at a 90° angle to each other. The first plate has in its center a cutout of 45x45. All plates are 10mm thick | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation concept (only with the provided functions)

1. Establish the first plate (horizontal in the XY-plane, 10 mm thick in +Z).
   • block(): x_size=140, y_size=140, z_size=10  
   • basepoint (x,y,z)=(0,0,0)  
   • subtraction=False   → this forms the initial solid.

2. Add the second plate, standing vertically along the YZ-plane, 10 mm thick in +X, so it meets the first plate at the common edge Y-axis/Z-axis corner.
   • block(): x_size=10, y_size=140, z_size=140  
   • basepoint (x,y,z)=(0,0,0) (the two plates therefore intersect in the 10 mm-thick volume 0≤x≤10, 0≤y≤140, 0≤z≤10, giving a rigid L-corner)  
   • subtraction=False

3. Cut the 45 mm × 45 mm opening through the center of the first plate.
   • The plate’s center in XY is (70,70).  
   • Opening basepoint: (70 − 22.5, 70 − 22.5, 0) = (47.5, 47.5, 0).  
   • block(): x_size=45, y_size=45, z_size=10 (same thickness as the plate)  
   • subtraction=True

After these three block-calls the geometry consists of two 140 × 140 plates at 90° with a centered 45 × 45 cut-out in the horizontal plate and both solids cleanly fused along their 10 mm-thick common edge.
